faqs.answer: About 32 minutes at 400F for bone-in thighs that roast for 40 minutes in the oven. Boneless thighs take about 20 minutes. Start checking at 28 minutes for bone-in.
faqs.question: How long do chicken thighs take in the air fryer?

faqs.answer: Bone-in thighs do, because the bone insulates the meat. Boneless thighs cook in about the same time as a boneless breast.
faqs.question: Do thighs take longer than breasts?

faqs.answer: Skin side up. The heat comes from above, so skin that faces up crisps. Pat it dry first, and do not crowd the basket.
faqs.question: Should thighs be skin side up or down?

faqs.answer: Yes, and many cooks prefer them around 175F, where the texture is better. 165F is the safety minimum. Past that is a taste choice.
faqs.question: Can I cook thighs past 165F?

faqs.question: Do I flip chicken thighs?

felicityNote: Thighs are the chicken I reach for on a tired night. They forgive a late timer, they forgive a hot fryer, and the skin always crisps.

parts.meaning: The air fryer runs hotter than the dial says, because the fan pushes hot air straight onto the food. Dropping 25F keeps the skin from burning before the meat cooks.
The fan cooks food about 20 percent faster than still oven air, so the air fryer time is four fifths of the oven time.
The check-at time is 70 percent of the oven time. Open the basket then, look, and check the temperature.
The safe internal temperature for chicken, measured in the thickest part, away from the bone.

formula.text: Air fryer temp = oven temp minus 25F. Air fryer time = oven time × 0.8. Check at = oven time × 0.7. For chicken thighs at 425F for 40 minutes: 400F for 32 minutes, check at 28 minutes.

howToSteps.name: Read the oven settings
howToSteps.text: Find the temperature and time in your recipe. Bone-in thighs usually roast at 425F for 40 minutes.

howToSteps.name: Convert both numbers
howToSteps.text: Take 25F off the temperature and take 20 percent off the time. 425F for 40 minutes becomes 400F for 32 minutes.

howToSteps.name: Dry and season
howToSteps.text: Pat the skin dry, season, and load the thighs skin side up in a single layer.

howToSteps.name: Cook and check
howToSteps.text: Start checking at 28 minutes, and pull the thighs when the thickest part reads 165F.

title: Oven to Air Fryer: Chicken Thighs
tutorial: Thighs are the most forgiving chicken in the air fryer. Bone-in thighs that roast at 425F for 40 minutes air fry at 400F for 32 minutes, and the skin comes out crisper than the oven manages. Start checking at 28 minutes.

Dark meat forgives what breast does not. A thigh that cooks a few minutes past done stays juicy, because the fat and the connective tissue keep it moist. That makes thighs the chicken to learn the air fryer on. The converted time is a starting point, and a few minutes either way still gives you dinner.

Bone-in takes longer than boneless, and the bone is the reason. Bone insulates the meat around it, so a bone-in thigh needs the full converted time while a boneless thigh finishes sooner. The presets cover both. If you are converting a recipe, check whether it says bone-in or boneless before you trust the time.

Skin side up, and do not move them. Thighs go in skin side up, and the skin crisps under the heat from above. Flip them once halfway if the recipe says so, but skin that starts up and stays up comes out crisper. Pat the skin dry first, the same as wings.

The thermometer still decides. Thighs are done at 165F in the thickest part, away from the bone. Some cooks take dark meat higher, toward 175F, for better texture, and that is a taste choice, not a safety rule. The safety number is 165F, and the thermometer is the only honest test.
